NAME

md_docs_2recording - Recording session audio and ASCII video

--render-file recording.mp4 records the session's ASCII video and its audio mix in client, discovery, and mirror modes. Mirror is a solo session: it records local audio without playing the microphone back through the speakers.

Local capture and media playback follow --audio-capture-source:

  • auto: file/URL audio when available, otherwise the microphone.
  • mic: the microphone.
  • Media: file/URL audio.
  • both: microphone and file/URL audio mixed together.

Network sessions also record received participant audio. Speaker playback remains separate from recording, so recording does not consume playback or outgoing audio buffers. Local file audio plays through the speakers in mirror mode; in a call it is sent to other participants and included in the recording.

When --file or --url contains only audio, the selected webcam supplies the video. The webcam is opened when capture starts, rather than during metadata probing. The file retains its usual pause, seek, and loop controls. Without a usable webcam, capture reports an error identifying the selected camera.

Examples:

ascii-chat mirror --render-file solo.mp4
ascii-chat mirror --file music.wav --render-file music-with-webcam.mp4
ascii-chat client localhost --file clip.mp4 --render-file call.mp4
ascii-chat client localhost --file music.wav --audio-capture-source both --render-file call.mp4

Video containers such as MP4 and WebM support audio. Still images and GIF do not.

Use --render-font default, --render-font matrix, or an absolute font-file path to select the font for pixel output. Existing relative font files are accepted too. Explicit font-file failures stop rendering with an error rather than silently substituting the bundled default. Family-name aliases retain the platform's normal font-resolution policy.

Apple HVF fonts (OpenType/TrueType containers with hvgl outlines) require FreeType 2.15 or newer built with HVF enabled, plus macOS 15.4 or iOS 18.4 or newer at runtime. Apple builds report the FreeType capability at configuration time; source builds use FreeType 2.15. Older FreeType packages or SDKs still support ordinary fonts and reject unsupported HVF input at runtime. The iOS dependency can be cross-built with Xcode's Clang and a recent iOS SDK while retaining an older deployment target; HVF remains unavailable on older OS versions. Windows, Linux, and browser builds do not support Apple HVF fonts and report unsupported font formats. Ordinary TrueType/OpenType fonts and the bundled fonts remain available on all platforms.

Audio is mixed at 48 kHz mono and clipped after summing inputs. Temporary missing samples become silence, and subsequent samples resume normally. Live video uses elapsed session time across source changes and pauses. Stdin conversion retains frame-count timing.

The recording regression tests include PCM mixing, microphone and file worker paths, independent playback/transmission queues, audio-only webcam selection, mixed encoded audio, encoder-tail flushing, and live frame timing. A separate mirror and two-client test checks the file tone in mirror output, both input tones in each call output, and A/V synchronization: 

uv run --project tests/ascii_chat_tests --frozen python -m pytest tests/python/integration/recording --ascii-chat-binary build/bin/ascii-chat

Media transition behavior

All native client, discovery and mirror sessions use the shared capture/display pipeline. Browser mirror, client and discovery share useSessionRecording, LocalRecording and the AudioPipeline recording bus. Committed source changes do not create a new recording or reset its session clock.

Paused native recordings emit the last raster until recording ends, even if playback never resumes. Their frame freshness counter remains unchanged. At normal file EOF, native file recording still finalizes rather than extending the last frame indefinitely. Stdin retains its frame-count conversion semantics. Browser pause/seek preserves the stable destination audio track so changing file tracks does not end the encoder. A repeated source notification for the same media element does not recapture or stop its tracks.

Browser exports remain bounded to ten minutes / 128 MiB, with a ten-second finalization watchdog. Encoder failure produces an error rather than a partial download; a subsequent recording starts with fresh failure state. Browser source controls and native capture policy are distinct host adapters around their shared session APIs; MCP is a bounded render tool, not a live session controller.

Focused regression coverage:

  • pytest tests/python/integration/recording --ascii-chat-binary BINARY --recording-transitions-only: hardware-free paused-file finalization, synthetic A/V duration and playlist source switching with both tones retained in one recording.
  • tests/standalone/media/capture_open_test.c: retained paused recording frames, seek while paused, unchanged freshness, and existing load rollback/cancellation.
  • web/web/tests/network/audio-pipeline.test.ts: stable file tap through pause, seek, dynamic audio track replacement and failed replacement rollback.
  • web/web/tests/hooks/session-recording.test.tsx: disconnect/reconnect during preparation cannot resurrect a stale recording start.
  • web/web/tests/recording/local-recording.test.ts: final chunks, watchdog, cancellation, limits and recovery after encoder failure.

Hardware-specific camera availability, public URL extraction, and real browser codec output require their existing platform/browser smoke tests; synthetic unit fixtures do not establish those claims.
